blocks.prompt: 4 (a) A car is travelling along a straight road. At \(t = 0\) seconds, the car passes a point \(A\) with a velocity of 12 m/s, and this velocity is maintained up to \(t = 35\) seconds. The driver then applies the brakes, and the car decelerates uniformly, coming to rest at the point \(B\) at \(t = 40\) seconds. Sketch a velocity-time graph to illustrate the motion of the car.
blocks.explanation:
A sketch question: we turn the words into the shape of a velocity-time graph.
Given: constant 12 m/s for 35 s, then uniform deceleration to rest at 40 s.
Plan: constant velocity gives a horizontal line; uniform deceleration gives a straight falling line.
steps:
Given: v = 12 m/s from t = 0 to t = 35 s; uniform deceleration to v = 0 at t = 40 s.
To find: the velocity-time graph.
Method: Key Features of Velocity-Time Graph (7.1.5): a = 0 gives a horizontal line; a constant negative a gives a straight falling line.

First part: constant velocity
\[(0, 12) \text{ to } (35, 12)\]
Why: the velocity does not change, so the slope (acceleration) is zero and the line is horizontal.

Second part: uniform deceleration
\[(35, 12) \text{ to } (40, 0)\]
\[a = \dfrac{0 - 12}{40 - 35} = -2.4\text{ m/s}^2\]
Why: uniform deceleration means a constant negative slope, so the graph is a straight line falling to the time axis, where the car is at rest.

Check
\[12 - 2.4 \times 5 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: with v = u + at the velocity is zero exactly at t = 40 s, as the question says.
blocks.final_answer: A horizontal line at \(v = 12\) m/s from \(t = 0\) to \(t = 35\) s, then a straight line down to \(v = 0\) at \(t = 40\) s (a trapezium shape); see the figure.

answer_figure.alt: Velocity-time graph of the car: a horizontal line at v = 12 from t = 0 to t = 35, then a straight line down to v = 0 at t = 40; the area under it is a rectangle 420 plus a triangle 30.
answer_figure.caption: Question 4: velocity-time graph of the car from A to B (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 4 (b) A car is travelling along a straight road. At \(t = 0\) seconds, the car passes a point \(A\) with a velocity of 12 m/s, and this velocity is maintained up to \(t = 35\) seconds. The driver then applies the brakes, and the car decelerates uniformly, coming to rest at the point \(B\) at \(t = 40\) seconds. Find the displacement from \(A\) to \(B\).
blocks.explanation:
Displacement is the area under the velocity-time graph drawn in part (a).
Given: the trapezium with corners (0, 0), (0, 12), (35, 12), (40, 0).
Plan: area of the trapezium; check by rectangle plus triangle.
steps:
Given: the velocity-time graph of part (a).
To find: the displacement from A to B.
Method: displacement = area under the velocity-time graph (7.1.5); the region is a trapezium, area \(\frac{1}{2}(a + b)h\).

Sides of the trapezium
\[a = 40,\quad b = 35\]
\[h = 12\]
Why: the parallel sides are the bottom (0 to 40 on the time axis) and the top (0 to 35 at v = 12); the height is 12.

Area
\[x = \dfrac{1}{2}(40 + 35) \times 12\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}(75)(12) = 450\text{ m}\]
Why: area of a trapezium.

Check: rectangle plus triangle
\[12 \times 35 + \tfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12\]
\[= 420 + 30 = 450 \;\checkmark\]
Why: steady driving gives a rectangle and uniform braking gives a triangle.
